title: Depression and associated factors among parents of children diagnosed with cancer at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
central_claims: The published abstract reports 72.4% parental depression in 275 TASH participants and associations with single parenting, income, prior depression and support source.
The observational study recommends early identification and support; it does not establish intervention efficacy or causation.

source_manifest.title: Depression and associated factors among parents of children diagnosed with cancer at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
source_manifest.finding: Abstract reports 72.4% prevalence, although listed severity percentages sum to 23.3%; associations reported, not causal effects. Original journal full text inaccessible.

source_manifest.title: Depression and Associated Factors Among Parents Who Have Children Diagnosed with Cancer at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia 2017
source_manifest.finding: Related thesis by the same first author and supervisors reports the four severity categories summing to 23.3%, acknowledges limited sample and cross-sectional inference. Dates and some adjusted estimates differ from the journal abstract, so this is not silently substituted for the journal full text.

source_manifest.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prevalence of Depression Among Caregivers of Cancer Patients
source_manifest.finding: Pan and Lin include Mekonnen 2020, n=275, BDI, prevalence 23.30% in the 85-study analysis producing pooled 25.14%; this differs from the original headline 72.4%.

source_manifest.title: Health and economic impact of caregiving on informal caregivers of people with chronic diseases in sub-Saharan Africa: A systematic review
source_manifest.finding: Independent regional synthesis includes target as reference64 and uses its BDI estimate in a reported depression range of 26–72.4%.

source_manifest.title: Association of Family-Centered Care With Psychological Distress Among Caregivers of Children With Cancer at a Tertiary-Level Hospital in Ethiopia
source_manifest.finding: 384 caregivers, K10 psychological distress 33.6%; cites target 72.4% as background but studies a different outcome and excludes pre-existing mental illness. Not a direct reproduction.

source_manifest.title: Predictors of Depressive Symptoms Among Parents of Children With Cancer in Ethiopia
source_manifest.finding: Independent Jimma sample n122 reports 60.7% depressive symptoms; monthly income not significant, unlike original income association. Different setting and design limit direct contradiction.

answers.rationale: Newer Ethiopian samples confirm a burden of symptoms, but do not explicitly verify the original prevalence and factor set; Jimma finds no significant income predictor.
TASH parental-depression estimates and associations: No independent reproduction of the specific result was located.
The larger 2024 TASH sample measures K10 distress rather than the original BDI depression and uses different exclusions, so its 33.6% does not directly test the original 72.4%.
The syntheses use conflicting prevalence values (23.3% versus 72.4%); no authoritative reconciliation of the headline estimate and associated-factor claims was located.
TASH parental-depression estimates and associations: No later test of the original limitations demonstrating retained usefulness was located.
TASH parental-depression estimates and associations: No substantive extension by an independent team was established.

Independent 2022 quantitative and 2024 regional syntheses actually extract this study’s findings for their analyses. The two teams and calendar years establish reuse; the 2024 reuse is over three years later. Their inconsistent prevalence extraction limits validation.

research.summary: Substantive independent synthesis reuse is established in 2022 and 2024. Validation remains uncertain because prevalence extraction is inconsistent and newer Ethiopian studies use different measures or find different predictors. Original journal assessed at abstract scope.
